title: Primer validation for A. hydrophila.
author: Sang Hyuk Lee
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.title: Contaminate pipette tips
steps.instruction: Expose all pipette tips (control and experimental groups) to DNA extracts of Aeromonas hydrophila (ATCC‑23211) to create contaminated samples.

steps.title: Detergent cleaning and steam
steps.instruction: Immerse contaminated tips in 2.5 % Alconox® solution, rinse as appropriate, then subject them to steam decontamination.

substeps.instruction: Place tips in the solution for the recommended contact time.
Rinse tips to remove detergent residue.
Expose tips to steam for the standard cycle.

steps.title: Ozone exposure (low dose)
steps.instruction: Expose a set of contaminated tips to ozone vapor at 250 PPM · minute.

steps.title: Ozone exposure (high dose)
steps.instruction: Expose another set of contaminated tips to ozone vapor at 14 400 PPM · minute.

steps.title: Cold atmospheric plasma treatment
steps.instruction: Invert tips (tip end facing the plasma flame) and expose them to cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) for 1 minute.

steps.title: Assess decontamination by qPCR
steps.instruction: Extract any remaining DNA from each tip group and perform real‑time quantitative PCR (qPCR) to calculate turnover ratio and log reduction; record the observed values.

substeps.instruction: Extract genomic material from each tip after treatment.
Run qPCR using appropriate primers for A. hydrophila.
Calculate turnover ratio and log reduction for each decontamination method.
Record results: Detergent/steam – turnover 95.9 %, log reduction 5.943; Ozone 14 400 PPM·minute – turnover 98.4 %, log reduction 4.511; CAP – turnover 68.3 %, log reduction 4.002.
